mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at t-0w signals a reopening of commuting routines that should raise retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks as weekday out-of-home activity normalizes.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not average above its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining above their t-1w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in RESIDENTIAL mobility relative to recent weeks implies more time spent outside home, which should translate into higher discretionary shopping and dining activity and lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15 points above baseline after being at or above 17 points in the prior two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops from its prior two-week range into the low-teens above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both strengthen together, the combined increase in commuting and foot traffic creates a larger retail spillover than either series alone, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both trend upward from the decision point.

mechanism_narrative: A large deterioration in TRANSIT relative to recent weeks is a restriction or disruption signal that suppresses discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC should decline over the next four weeks if transit remains depressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -65 and stays there for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after TRANSIT breaches the low-transit threshold and remains near that level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward move in PARKS mobility indicates warmer-weather outdoor substitution that competes with indoor retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next one to two weeks when park usage surges.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points week-on-week from a negative or near-zero level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 7 to 14 days after a sharp PARKS surge instead of softening.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL falls, households are reallocating trips from home-based activity to essential errands, which should spill over into more retail outings and raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of very low TRANSIT and persistently weak WORKPLACES mobility indicates continued suppression of discretionary movement; if this regime persists, retail activity should remain below its recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean while TRANSIT remains below -60 and WORKPLACES remains more than 30 points below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after a prior weak week is an early normalization cue that typically precedes broader consumer activity, so RETAIL_REC should move higher within one week once the rebound is sustained.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive after being negative in the previous week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the week after GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive.
